alternativeSelection.assessment: uses mathematics and computation to study physical processes in the Earth system and the design of renewable energy systems. The programme lists biophysics interests, but general biomedical courses and image processing do not sustain a progression in physical measurement of living systems or medical instrumentation. Groningen also requires mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics and experimental laboratory work.

audience.programmeDescription: Students combine mathematical modelling and computing with mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics and experiments. They complete a minor and a research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination uses mathematics and computation to study physical processes in the Earth system and the design of renewable energy systems. Groningen also requires mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics and experimental laboratory work.
